valuation_philosophy.model_type: REIT AFFO capitalization at cost of equity (5-year explicit AFFO path + Gordon terminal capped at 16x AFFO), NOT a WACC-based owner-FCF DCF; NTA x exit-P/NTA reported as a memo cross-check, not blended
valuation_philosophy.rationale: Vital is an IAS 40 fair-value healthcare property trust (33 hospitals/ambulatory assets, NZ$3.5bn, 19-year WALE, 63% CPI-linked rent), internally managed since 31-Dec-2025. Statutory net income is revaluation noise (+303.5m FY22, -152.4m FY23, -24.8m FY26 after a 214.7m one-off internalisation payment) and the CSV free cash flow is OCF less DEVELOPMENT capex (structurally negative: -377m FY22) -- neither is a flow to capitalize. The Trust's own key metric is AFFO (note 12: operating profit ex non-cash/one-off items, after net finance cost and current tax, less maintenance capex). AFFO is an EQUITY-level flow, so it is discounted at the cost of equity and net debt (1,414m) is never subtracted -- doing so would charge the 1.4bn of borrowings twice. Explicit five-year path is built bottom-up from NPI, G&A, net finance cost, current tax and maintenance capex (assumptions[scenario].component_build_nzdm) so that three effects the headline 11.50 cpu hides are modelled rather than extrapolated: (1) the year-end unit count is 807.1m, not the 756.0m weighted average the 11.50 cpu is struck on -- FY26 AFFO on year-end units is 10.77 cpu; (2) ~178m of NZ tax losses from the internalisation payment (49.9m deferred tax asset recognised FY26) shelter current tax for roughly four years and then run out, so the terminal year is fully taxed; (3) ~15m/yr of capitalised development interest moves to the P&L as RDX Gold Coast, Grace Hospital and Boulcott complete, only partly offset by their rent. The unit count is held flat: DRP issuance (~7m units/yr) is matched by the cash it retains for development, and the FY26 235m placement/UPP is already in the 807.1m. SBC (LTIP ~1.0m/yr, added back in the Trust's AFFO) is treated as a cash cost on the house basis; the street basis adds it back (+0.02/unit). Weights 25/50/25: bear held above the 15% house default because gearing is 39.6%, 20% of debt is unhedged with hedges rolling in ~2.6 years, and top-5 tenants are 65% of rent in a sector that produced an operator collapse (Healthscope) in 2025.

warnings: REIT AFFO-capitalization model: reported NetIncome/EPS (fair-value revaluations) and the CSV FreeCashFlow (OCF less development capex, structurally negative) are excluded as drivers by design. P/E, EV/EBITDA and FCF-yield sanity checks are inapplicable; use P/AFFO and P/NTA.

AFFO is post-interest. Net debt of 1,414.0m (borrowings 1,427.8m less cash 13.8m at 30-Jun-2026) is NEVER subtracted; inputs.net_debt is 0 for the engine bridge and the true figure is in inputs.net_debt_memo.

Per-unit anchor: the 11.50 cpu FY26 AFFO is struck on 755.951m weighted-average diluted units; the Trust has 807.127m units on issue after the Dec-2025 placement/UPP. All forward per-unit values divide by 807.127m -- FY26 AFFO on that count is 10.77 cpu, so the base FY27 11.65 cpu is +8% on a like-for-like count, not +1%.

Tax shelter is finite: FY26 current tax fell to 7.9m (FY25 15.5m) because the 214.7m internalisation payment is deductible (49.9m DTA on tax losses recognised). The model shelters FY27-FY29, steps up in FY30 and fully taxes FY31 (17.0m base). Holding the shelter in perpetuity would add ~0.20/unit and is wrong.

The base case sits BELOW the market price (1.58 vs 1.92) and below NTA (0.66x). At 1.92 the units yield 6.0% on FY26 AFFO and 5.1% on the 9.75 cpu distribution; the price is consistent with a ~7.5-8% cost of equity or a re-rating to ~0.95x NTA (see required_return_table and the NTA cross-check at exit 0.95x = bull). This model does not underwrite that re-rating.

Distribution cover: 9.75 cpu is 84% of base FY27 AFFO but exceeds bear-case AFFO from FY30 (9.65 cpu) -- the bear path includes a cut to 8.0 cpu. FY27 guidance is 9.75 cpu, 'reviewed as development leasing progresses'.

Rate sensitivity: 80% of borrowings hedged at 3.45% with ~2.6yr average hedge term; weighted average interest rate 5.06% (FY25 4.90%). RBNZ resumed hiking in Jul-2026. Each +50bp on the unhedged 20% plus roll-off is ~2-3m of AFFO (~0.3 cpu).
AUD exposure: ~67-69% of the portfolio is Australian; FY26 AFFO was helped by AUD strength (Q3 update). The model is in NZD with no explicit FX path.
Terminal value is 63-74% of value across scenarios -- normal for a capitalization model, but the result moves ~0.10/unit per 50bp of cost of equity (see sensitivity).

inputs.share_count_basis: 807.127m units on issue at 30-Jun-2026 (FY26 annual report note 10: 678.896m opening + 7.265m DRP + 120.966m placement/UPP). NOT the 755.951m weighted-average diluted count in the Metrics CSV, which is the FY26 AFFO-per-unit denominator. Held FLAT: DRP (~7m units/yr) retains matching cash for development; no further raise assumed; LTIP dilution immaterial (~0.4m units).
inputs.net_debt_note: Set to 0 for the valuation bridge because AFFO is already after net finance cost -- subtracting borrowings again would double-count leverage (SKILL.md REIT rule; ARG/PCT/IPL precedent). True net debt is in net_debt_memo for audit and the units backfill script.
inputs.gearing_note: Debt to total assets 39.6% at 30-Jun-2026 (Trust Deed basis; 42.1% FY25). Interest cover 2.74x. Weighted average debt maturity 4.3 years, no maturities before April 2028; 80% hedged at 3.45% average fixed; WAIR 5.06% (FY25 4.90%). Liquidity 276.2m (88.5m after committed development spend).
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026 AFFO 86.918m (note 12) -- the flow this model capitalizes. It is post-interest and post-current-tax and includes the internalisation tax benefit (current tax 7.9m vs 15.5m FY25). Not an owner-FCF figure; reported_fcf below is retained only for auditability.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: OCF 85.191 less total investing capex 75.818 (development + maintenance). Structurally meaningless for a developing REIT; not used.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report note 12 (share based payments expense 429k added back to FFO; equity statement 533k). Post-internalisation LTIP only -- pre-FY26 the Northwest incentive fee was unit-settled (6.6m FY24, 14.9m FY23) but was a manager fee, not employee SBC. House basis charges ~1.0m/yr inside G&A (component build); street basis adds it back. sbc_pct_path is 0 because the charge sits inside the AFFO margin, not as a separate engine deduction.
inputs.sbc_treatment: house = cash cost inside g_and_a_incl_sbc; street = added back (Trust's own AFFO definition)
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income 1.581m is netted inside AFFO (net finance cost). No separate deduction: the Trust has no net cash.
inputs.model: REIT AFFO capitalization at cost of equity (dcf-methods routing table, REIT row)
inputs.notes: Model: AFFO capitalization at cost of equity, routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md REIT row (IAS 40 fair-value property trust). Owner-FCF DCF is meaningless here: FCF is structurally negative from development capex and net income is revaluation noise. Same family as ARG.NZ, PCT.NZ, IPL.NZ; unlike PCT the NTA leg is a memo cross-check rather than a 50/50 blend, because Vital has traded below NTA every FY-end since FY22 (0.71-0.85x) and an AFFO-only value keeps the dashboard slider engine reproducible. Currency: statements and quote both NZD (67% of assets are AUD -- translation risk noted, no FX bridge needed). Price 1.92 from Yahoo at the 18-Sep-2026 NZX close. Balance sheet, units and NTA from the FY2026 annual report (30-Jun-2026, published 13-Aug-2026). Weights 25/50/25.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity (not WACC): NZ 10-year government bond ~4.5% (Sep-2026, RBNZ hiking) + 0.75 beta x 6.0% NZ ERP = 9.0%, +0.5% for 39.6% gearing / 20% unhedged debt, top-5 tenant concentration (65% of rent) and AUD translation = 9.5% base; 9.0% bull; 10.5% bear. 0.75-1.0pp below the 10.25-10.5% used for PCT.NZ (office) and IPL.NZ (Woolworths concentration, external manager): healthcare, 19-year CPI-linked WALE, internalised management. NZD flows discounted at an NZD rate.

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_basis: AFFO total (the capitalized flow); reported FCF is negative in most years and has no CAGR
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case terminal AFFO-per-unit growth (CPI-linked rent growth less interest and tax drift). Historical AFFO/unit CAGR is -0.1% (5yr) and +0.7% (8yr): total AFFO grew 8.6%/yr FY21-26 but almost all of it was absorbed by unit issuance and higher interest cost. Equity CAGR is not used -- it is fair-value revaluation plus equity raises.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.3% vs revenue 8.9% and AFFO/unit -0.1%: divergence >30% is expected for an IAS 40 trust (revaluations, equity raises) and is not a data error. AFFO-per-unit is the series that matters and it is flat.
historical_growth.notes: FY22-FY26 like-for-like NPI growth 2.8/3.6/3.7/3.7/4.1%. Net interest expense rose from 27.7m (FY21) to 54.3m (FY26). NTA/unit peaked at 3.34 (FY22) and fell to 2.41 on 470m of cumulative revaluation losses FY23-25 plus the ~6% internalisation dilution.

bear.engine_note: Component fields are the dashboard slider engine's vocabulary mapped onto the AFFO model: revenue = gross property income (rentals + expense recoveries), ebitda_margin_path = AFFO / gross property income, and every other component knob (SBC%, D&A%, capex%, WC capture, cash tax, lease cost) is 0 because tax, interest, G&A and maintenance capex are already netted inside AFFO via component_build_nzdm. wacc holds the COST OF EQUITY: AFFO is post-interest, so it discounts at CoE and net_debt is 0 in the bridge (see inputs.net_debt_note).
bear.rationale: An Australian private-hospital operator stress event (the sector saw Healthscope's 2025 collapse and margin pressure at Healthe Care/Aurora) leads to rent relief and re-leasing downtime: NPI grows only 1.5%/yr. Rates stay higher for longer (RBNZ resumed hiking Jul-2026) so the hedge roll-off lifts net finance cost 6%/yr to 71.5m. AFFO falls to 8.8 cpu by FY31 and the 9.75 cpu distribution is cut from FY29. CoE 10.5%, g 2.0% (Gordon 12.0x). Cap-rate softening would also cut NTA (-2%/yr in the cross-check, exit 0.65x) but does not enter the AFFO leg directly.

base.engine_note: Component fields are the dashboard slider engine's vocabulary mapped onto the AFFO model: revenue = gross property income (rentals + expense recoveries), ebitda_margin_path = AFFO / gross property income, and every other component knob (SBC%, D&A%, capex%, WC capture, cash tax, lease cost) is 0 because tax, interest, G&A and maintenance capex are already netted inside AFFO via component_build_nzdm. wacc holds the COST OF EQUITY: AFFO is post-interest, so it discounts at CoE and net_debt is 0 in the bridge (see inputs.net_debt_note).
base.rationale: FY27 AFFO 94.0m (11.65 cpu on 807.1m year-end units; FY26 reported 11.50 cpu on the 756.0m weighted count, ~11.6-11.7 cpu H2 FY26 run-rate on year-end units). NPI +4.8% FY27 then fading to +3.9% (like-for-like CPI/market reviews 3.5-4.1% as FY22-FY26, plus Grace Hospital (PC 6-Jul-2026), RDX Gold Coast full year and the $187.7m committed pipeline at a 6.3% yield on cost, net of FY26 divestments). G&A 18.8m incl ~1.0m LTIP (internal cost base at the disclosed 0.53% annualised MER, vs 23.2m FY25 with the Northwest base fee). Net cash finance cost 58.0m rising to 68.5m: debt grows with development, ~15m of FY26 capitalised interest moves to P&L as RDX/Grace/Boulcott complete, and the 80%-hedged book (3.45% swaps, ~2.6yr) reprices upward from FY29. Current tax 3.0m FY27-FY29 while the ~178m of internalisation tax losses (49.9m DTA recognised FY26) shelter NZ income, then 8.0m FY30 and 17.0m FY31 -- the terminal year is FULLY TAXED; perpetuating the shelter would add ~0.20/unit and is the error this build guards against. Cost of equity 9.5% (NZ 10yr ~4.5% + 0.75 beta x 6% ERP + 0.5% for 40% gearing, top-5 tenant concentration 65% and AUD exposure). Terminal growth 2.5% (CPI-linked rent less capex/tax drift); Gordon 14.6x AFFO (6.8% exit AFFO yield) binds below the 16x cap.

bull.engine_note: Component fields are the dashboard slider engine's vocabulary mapped onto the AFFO model: revenue = gross property income (rentals + expense recoveries), ebitda_margin_path = AFFO / gross property income, and every other component knob (SBC%, D&A%, capex%, WC capture, cash tax, lease cost) is 0 because tax, interest, G&A and maintenance capex are already netted inside AFFO via component_build_nzdm. wacc holds the COST OF EQUITY: AFFO is post-interest, so it discounts at CoE and net_debt is 0 in the bridge (see inputs.net_debt_note).
bull.rationale: Internalised platform delivers on its promise: NPI +5.7%/yr (developments lease at 6.3%+, market reviews positive, AUD firm), capital-partnership fee income builds to 7.5m, G&A held near 18.5m, funding cost eases (rates cut, refinancing margins improve) so net finance cost grows only 3%/yr. Tax shelter used more slowly on a larger deduction base; terminal still fully taxed at 16.0m. AFFO reaches 14.1 cpu by FY31; distributions lifted from FY29 to 10.5 cpu. CoE 9.0%, g 3.0%; the 16x cap binds (Gordon would be 17.2x) -- this is roughly the 17-19x AFFO the units traded at in FY24-FY25 and well below the 21-24x of FY22-FY23.

bear.enterprise_value_note: Equity-level capitalized value (AFFO is post-interest); labelled enterprise_value only for the output contract. Nothing is subtracted to reach equity_value.

nta_cross_check.method: PV of 5 years of DPU at CoE + PV of FY2031 NTA/unit x exit P/NTA (memo only, NOT blended into intrinsic_value)

entry_price.basis: Price at which buying today, collecting the projected AFFO for five years and exiting at a terminal value REBUILT AT THE 15% HURDLE (min(Gordon@15%, 16x AFFO_FY31)) returns a 15% IRR. No net-debt term: AFFO is post-interest. Weighted across scenarios with the same 25/50/25 weights as intrinsic value.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, 16x AFFO_FY31)). The 9.5% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price. At the 1.92 price the base path implies a cost of equity of roughly 7.5-8%.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Base AFFO path held constant. Rows = cost of equity 7.5-11.5%, columns = terminal growth 1.5-3.5%. NZD per unit. Cells where the 16x cap binds are flat across the growth axis (whole 7.5% row; 8.5% row from g=2.5%).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25. Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 25%: 39.6% gearing with 20% of debt unhedged and hedges rolling in ~2.6 years while the RBNZ is hiking, 65% of rent from five hospital operators in a sector that produced an operator collapse in 2025, and a newly internalised platform in its first full year. Bull 25%: the internalisation, refinancing and first revaluation gain in three years are real, and the units traded at 17-24x AFFO for four of the last five FY-ends.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band is only 0.018/unit wide (LTIP ~1.0m/yr); the price sits far above both, so band_position >100% simply restates that the market pays more than either basis.

market_context.consensus_target_note: Qualitative analyst's web research found an average broker target ~NZ$2.10; this model's weighted value is 1.54 because it fully taxes the terminal year and caps the exit multiple at 16x.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.checks_replaced: model is affo: P/E and EV/EBITDA trip rules do not apply; the historical table is reported for context only
